_doc: How the rival Houses' heads look and talk (systems/rivalHouses.js persona, systems/rivalAudience.js lines). A head's MANNER comes from their first trait: proud → haughty, courtly → silken, scheming → soft, grasping → brisk, homebody → plain. STANCE comes from their regard for you (−feud + what they remember): warm ≥ 30, civil ≥ −10, cold ≥ −50, else hostile. Each list is picked by hash of the day and the head, so the same meeting reads the same. Placeholders: {you} your name, {yourHouse} your House, {first} their first name, {myHouse} their House, {seat} their seat, {passion} their passion, {other} another House, {place} a town, {good} a good, {gold} an amount, {realm} a realm, {child} a child's name, {days} days. *Asterisks* are stage directions.

hairYoung: with a young man's first beard
features: a hawk hooded on the wrist
a cough they try to hide
a jeweled dagger they toy with
a limp from an old fall

passions.name: falconry
passions.line: My falcon took a heron on the wing last week. You should have seen it stoop.

passions.name: the hunt
passions.line: There is a boar in the woods above {seat} that has killed two of my hounds. I mean to have him.

passions.name: verse
passions.line: I have been writing verses. Badly, my wife says. She is right.

passions.name: dice
passions.line: I lost forty gold at dice last night to a tanner. A tanner!

passions.name: horses
passions.line: I have a grey mare out of the southern studs. Fastest thing on four legs between here and the sea.

passions.name: the faith
passions.line: I have endowed a chapel at {seat}. A man should think of his soul.

passions.name: chess
passions.line: Do you play chess? No? A pity. You would understand me better.

passions.name: building
passions.line: I am raising a new hall at {seat}. Oak beams, a gallery for the musicians.

passions.name: the sea
passions.line: I would sooner be on a deck than in a saddle. The sea is honest.

passions.name: old books
passions.line: I bought a chronicle of the old kings from a monk. Half of it is lies, the best half.

memoryLabels.desecrated: the bones of their fathers you scattered
memoryLabels.cryptRobbed: the crypt of their fathers you robbed
memoryLabels.bonesReturned: the bones you brought back to their crypt
memoryLabels.repelled: your failed attack on their retinue
memoryLabels.spokeForThem: how you spoke for them at court
memoryLabels.loanDemanded: how you pressed them for a debt

warm: *inclines their head, just so* {you}. You may approach.
Ah, {you}. One of the few worth my time on these roads.
civil: *looks you over from the saddle* {yourHouse}. You wished to speak with {myHouse}?
Well. {you}. I suppose the road is common to all.
cold: *does not dismount* You have a moment. Use it well.
{yourHouse}. *the name sounds like something spat out* Speak.
hostile: *a gloved hand rests on the sword* You dare stand in my road?
I would not cross the street to piss on {yourHouse} if it burned. What do you want?

warm: *a warm smile, both hands open* {you}! The roads are kind today.
My dear {you}. I was only just speaking of you, and well.
civil: *a courtier's bow* {you}. What a pleasant surprise. Mostly pleasant.
{yourHouse}, on the open road. How the world turns.
cold: *the smile stays, the eyes do not* {you}. How… unexpected.
Ah. {yourHouse}. One hears so much about you at court. Very little of it kind.
hostile: *the smile is a blade* {you}. I had hoped the roads would be safer this season.
How brave of you, to come so close. Or how foolish. Say your piece.

warm: *speaks low, almost fondly* {you}. We should talk more, you and I.
Friend {you}. Sit a moment. Tell me what you know.
civil: *watches you with half-closed eyes* {you}. I wondered when our roads would cross.
*quietly* {yourHouse}. I know a great deal about you. Tell me something I don't.
cold: *says nothing for a long moment, then* …{you}.
*a soft voice, a hard face* You have walked a long way to stand within reach of my men.
hostile: *barely above a whisper* I have been thinking about you, {you}. Every night.
*smiles without warmth* Strange. My men said you would avoid this road.

warm: {you}! Good. Business is good, the roads are dry. What do you need?
Ha, {you}. Walk with me, I am pricing wool.
civil: {yourHouse}. I have a cart of {good} going bad in this heat. Be quick.
*glances at your purse before your face* {you}. Talk.
cold: Every hour I stand here costs me money. What is it?
{yourHouse}. You cost me a good deal at market. Say what you want.
hostile: You have no idea what your meddling has cost me. None. Get out of my road.
*counting coins, not looking up* If you came to beg, the answer is no. If you came to threaten, the answer is also no.

warm: {you}, well met! Come share the fire, there is stew.
*a broad grin* I hoped I would see you. How are your people?
civil: {you}. Fair road to you. What brings you?
*nods* {yourHouse}. I am bound home to {seat}, and glad of it.
cold: *folds their arms* {you}. I have nothing to say that you'll want to hear.
Say it plain, {you}. I've no patience for courtly talk.
hostile: You've got some nerve. Say what you came to say and be gone.
*spits* {yourHouse}. My father would have had you whipped from this road.

bereaved: *wears mourning black* My {parent} is a month in the ground. Forgive me if I am short.
*the black armband is new* We buried my {parent} at {seat}. The House is mine now. All of it.
attacked: *a fresh bandage on the arm* You have the gall to show your face, after what you did on the road?
*the retinue bristles at the sight of you* My men still bear the marks of your ambush.
insulted: *jaw tight* I have not forgotten your words. Nor has anyone who heard them.
shamed: *does not meet your eye* You need not gloat. I know how it went.
ousted: *sourly* You'll have heard, no doubt. {other} has the crown's ear now. A passing fancy.
poor: *the retinue looks thinner, the cloaks patched* These are lean days for {myHouse}. Lean days.
loss: *grumbling* I bought dear and sold cheap. Every fool in the market made money but me.
gloat: *a thin smile* You look a little lighter in the purse than when last we met.
triumph: *in high spirits* You find me on a good day, {you}. A very good day.
favour: *smoothing a new cloak* The crown has been generous. I find I like court.
wedding: *flushed with wine* My {child} is wed! There was dancing for three nights.
birth: *beaming* I have a new child, {you}. Named {child}. Loud as a bugle.
land: *pleased* I have bought land. Good land. Tenants who pay.
profit: *in a good humour* The {good} sold well. A fine week.
hunting: *the retinue rides armed, and close* You are a hard {you} to find.

recall.gift: Your gold reached my coffers. I have not decided what it bought you.
recall.parleyOk: Last time we spoke, you were almost reasonable.
recall.parleyFail: Last time you spoke to me, you wasted my afternoon.
recall.insult: I remember what you called me before the crowd.
recall.attacked: I remember the road where your men fell on mine.
recall.repelled: You tried your steel on my retinue once. You remember how that went.
recall.ambushBeaten: *colouring* We need not speak of the road.
recall.robbedYou: I hope the purse you lost to my men was not too dear to you.
recall.match: Our children are wed. That counts for something, even between us.
recall.flattered: You have a silver tongue. I have not decided whether I trust it.
recall.threatened: The last time we met, you threatened me. I do not forget threats.
recall.helped: You did me a service. I keep accounts of those, too.
recall.spokeForThem: You spoke for me at court. I have not forgotten.
recall.loanGiven: You lent me gold when I needed it. That was decently done.
recall.loanDemanded: You pressed me for coin in front of my own men.
recall.bloodPrice: The blood price you paid was fair. I have kept my side.
recall.duelYouWon: You bested me with the blade. I still feel it in this arm.
recall.duelYouLost: I drew first blood, the last time we crossed swords.
recall.declined: You refused my offer. I wonder that you came back.
recall.estateSold: You sold me good land at a fair price. Few can say that of you.
recall.truceBroken: *shifts in the saddle* There was a truce. Things happened.

haughty: *a long pause* …Very well. I will think less ill of you.
You speak better than I expected. Let it be calmer between us.
silken: *laughs softly* You are charming when you want something. Very well.
Peace? How refreshing. Let us try it, for a season.
soft: *nods slowly* Perhaps. Perhaps we have both been fools.
I will remember you said that. In the good way.
brisk: Fine. A feud is bad for trade anyway.
Fair words. I will take them, they cost me nothing.
plain: *sighs* Aye. Maybe it's gone on long enough.
That's plain spoken. I can respect that.

silken: *the smile thins* How very sincere. I am almost moved.
Darling {you}, you will have to try harder than that.
soft: You think I don't see what you are doing?
brisk: Talk is cheap. I don't deal in cheap.
plain: Pretty words. I've heard them before.
*shakes their head* No. Not after everything.

haughty: *a servant takes it; they do not look at it* Acceptable.
silken: Oh, you shouldn't have. *tucks it away at once*
How generous. I will speak warmly of you, for a week or two.
soft: *weighs the purse in one hand* And what does this buy, I wonder?
I'll take it. I won't forget who gave it.
brisk: *counts it, there and then* All there. Good.
That'll cover the tolls to {place}. My thanks.
plain: *surprised* I didn't expect that. Thank you.

haughty: Again? You think {myHouse} can be bought by the month?
silken: Another? My dear, people will talk.
soft: *narrows the eyes* Twice. Now I really wonder what you want.
brisk: I'll take it. But don't think it's buying what you think.

haughty: *goes white, then red* You will answer for that. By the gods, you will answer for it.
*a deathly calm* Say that again. I want my men to remember it exactly.
silken: *laughs, too loudly* How droll. Everyone heard that, did they? Good.
Oh, that will be all over court by Sunday. Thank you.
soft: *smiles, slowly* I will remember that. I will remember it for a very long time.
brisk: Insults cost nothing, and they're worth what they cost.
You'll pay for that. Not today, but you'll pay.
plain: *fist clenched* Say that again and we'll settle it here.

insultAgain: Again? You have no other song?
*wearily* You said that before. It was not clever then, either.

ok: *preens a little despite themselves* Well. You are not wholly without eyes.
*a reluctant smile* Flattery. And yet I find I don't mind it.
fail: Do you take me for a child, to be sweetened with honey?

cowed: *glances at your host and back* …There's no need for that. Let us both keep to our own roads for a while.
defiant: *laughs* Threats? I have more swords than you have friends.
Come and try it, then. I'll be at {seat}.

warm: Go well, {you}. My door at {seat} is open.
Fair roads. Send word if you need anything.
civil: *a curt nod* Until the next time.
hostile: Watch your back on the roads, {you}.
*to their men, loud enough to hear* Remember that face.

business.trade: I'm carrying {good} to {place}. Prices there are a scandal, which is to say: good for me.
business.buying: I'm bound for {place} to buy {good}. Don't you dare get there first.
business.court: I'm for court at {place}. One must be seen, or one is forgotten.
business.shadow: *evasively* I have business in {place}. Private business.
business.home: Home to {seat}. My bed, my dogs, my own roof.
business.invest: There's land for sale near {place}. Good land. Mine, soon.
business.none: Deciding where to go next. The roads are long.

ambition.wealth: I mean to see {myHouse} rich again, as rich as my grandfather's day. Richer.
ambition.land: Land is the only wealth that stays. I want more of it.
ambition.favour: A House without a crown's ear is a House no one remembers. I will be heard at court.
ambition.revenge: *looks straight at you* I have one ambition left, {you}. You know what it is.

topics.noNews: Nothing worth telling. The roads, the weather, the price of bread.
topics.familyNone: I have no wife, no children. Only the House.
topics.heirLine: {child} will have it all after me. Pray the gods give them better sense than I had.
topics.askYours: And your {child}? I hear they are coming along.

you.warm: I think you are better than your House's name, {you}. I didn't always.
you.civil: I think you are a rival. Nothing personal. Mostly.
you.cold: I think you have done {myHouse} more harm than you know.
you.hostile: I think about you more than I think about my own children. That should tell you.

topics.butBad: But I have not forgotten {reasons}, either.

otherHouse.ally: {other}? Family, now, near enough. Speak ill of them and you speak ill of me.
otherHouse.friend: {other} are decent people. We understand one another.
otherHouse.neutral: {other}? I don't think about them much.
otherHouse.enemy: {other} are snakes. I'd sooner deal with you than with them, and that's saying something.

bloodPrice.pitch: *looks at you a long while* There is a way to end the worst of this. {gold} gold, a blood price, paid now. And I call off my men for {days} days.
bloodPrice.accept: *takes the purse* It is done. For {days} days, {myHouse} keeps its blades sheathed. You have my word.
bloodPrice.decline: Then we go on as we are.

loan.pitch: *lowers the voice* I am short of coin this season. Lend me {gold} gold, and I'll repay {owed} in {days} days.
loan.accept: *clasps your forearm* I'll not forget this. {days} days.

speak.pitch: The court of {realm} listens to you. Speak for me there. It will cost you a little of their good opinion, and earn you a great deal of mine.
speak.accept: *genuinely moved* That's a real kindness. I won't forget it.
speak.decline: I see. Your own name first. As it should be, I suppose.

buyEstate.pitch: You hold {estate}, near {place}. I'll give you {gold} gold for it. More than it's worth.
buyEstate.accept: *shakes your hand* Good land. A good bargain for both of us.
buyEstate.decline: Your loss. The offer won't come again soon.

match.pitch: My {theirChild} is of an age, and so is your {yourChild}. Let them wed. I'll waive the dowry. Blood binds better than words.
match.accept: *embraces you, to everyone's surprise* Then we are kin, or near it!
match.decline: *hurt, then hiding it* As you like.

against.pitch: {other} wrong us both. Shame their lord to their face, or fall on their retinue. Do that, and our quarrel is all but done.
against.accept: *a slow smile* Good. I'll hear of it, wherever I am.
against.decline: Then you're no use to me in that.

duel.pitch: *draws the sword halfway* Enough words. Let us settle this with steel, first blood. Here, now, before both our people.
duel.decline: *sheathes the blade with contempt* I thought as much.
